newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Michelin aims at 10,000t Nigeria rubber production.
newsitem.headline: Michelin aims at 10,000t Nigeria rubber production.

text.p: With the acquisition of a new rubber estate Michelin hopes to double its Nigerian production to 10,000 tonnes in seven years when trees mature, a company official said on Monday.
The new plantation in southwestern Nigeria covers between 4,000 and 5,000 hectares.

"The increased production will serve our tyre factory in Port Harcourt and if world prices look good we will also be able to export," Ikay Afe, general manager of Michelin Plantations Group told Reuters.
Demand at Michelin's Nigerian tyre factory is currently 7,000 tonnes annually, with 2,000 tonnes of cup lump supplied by local smallholder rubber farmers.

Although Nigeria is Africa's largest natural rubber producer with an annual harvest of around 90,000 tonnes, it is gradually declining due to a failure to replant trees that are past their most productive best.
Nigerian smallholder-produced rubber also suffers a reputation for poor quality and sells at a discount of up to 20 percent on the world market.
